_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 6. Saadia-specific moves: בני אלאשראף = 'sons of the nobles' (rationalizes בני האלהים — not angels/divine beings, but nobility); בנאת אלעאמה = 'daughters of the commoners' (for בנות האדם); v.4 חראמא = 'illicitly' (Saadia adds — flags the union as forbidden); v.6 פתואעדהם אללה = 'God admonished/threatened them' (per Blau 6:6 — rationalizes וינחם, avoids divine regret); v.6 אוצל אלמשקה אלי' קלובהם = 'brought distress to THEIR hearts' (Saadia transfers ויתעצב אל לבו from God's heart to humans' hearts, preserving divine impassivity); v.3 לא ינג'מד רוחי = 'My spirit shall not endure' (per Blau 6:3); v.14 אלשמשאר = 'boxwood' (Saadia identifies גופר with shimshar).

translations.1: And when the people began to multiply upon the face of the earth, and daughters were born to them —
translations.2: the sons of the nobles saw the daughters of the commoners — that they were beautiful — and they took for themselves wives from all whom they chose.
translations.3: And God said: 'My spirit shall not endure in these people forever, for they are corporeal; and their span shall be one hundred and twenty years.'
translations.4: And the giants were in the earth in that time; and also after that, when the sons of the nobles entered upon the daughters of the commoners illicitly, and they bore to them — these are the giants who from of old were men of name.
translations.5: And when God saw that the wickedness of the people had multiplied upon the earth, and that every notion of the thoughts of their hearts was pure wickedness all the time —
translations.6: God admonished them — since He had made them upon the earth — and brought distress to their hearts.
translations.7: Then God said: 'I shall wipe away the people whom I created from the face of the earth — from human to beast, to creeping thing, and to wild creature and bird of the sky — for I admonished them when I created them.'
translations.8: But Noah found favor before God.
translations.9: This is the exposition of the offspring of Noah. And Noah was a righteous man, sound in his generations; in obedience to God did Noah walk.
translations.10: And Noah begot three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
translations.11: And the earth was corrupted before God; and the earth was filled with injustice.
translations.12: And He saw it, when it was corrupted — for every corporeal one had corrupted his way upon it.
translations.13: And God said to Noah: 'The end of every corporeal one has drawn near before Me — for the earth has been filled with injustice on their account; and behold, I am destroying them from it.
translations.14: Make for yourself an ark of boxwood; and make it in compartments; and pitch it within and without with bitumen.
translations.15: And this is the measure by which you shall make it: three hundred cubits its length, fifty cubits its breadth, and thirty cubits its height.
translations.16: And make for it a light-source, and to a cubit shall you complete it from the top; and set for it a door in its side. Lowest, second, and third stories shall you make it.
translations.17: And behold, I am bringing the flood of water upon the earth, to destroy every corporeal being in which is the breath of life, from beneath the sky; and everything that is upon the earth shall perish.
translations.18: And I shall establish My covenant with you; and you shall enter into the ark — you, and your sons, and your wife, and your sons' wives with you.
translations.19: And of every living thing, of all flesh — pairs of every kind shall you bring into the ark, that they may live with you; male and female shall they be.
translations.20: Of the bird according to its kinds, and of the beasts according to their kinds, and of the rest of the creeping things of the earth according to its kinds — pairs of every kind shall enter to you, that they may live.
translations.21: And you, take for yourself of every food that is eaten, and gather it to you; and it shall be for you and for them as food.
translations.22: And Noah did according to all that God had commanded him; so did he do.
